evals.prompt: Write an implementation plan for splitting the billing service out of the monolith. I want it as a file I can hand to an agent.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>-plan.md with new-plan.py, fills in the v2 sections, runs check-plan.py, pastes its output into Plan Self-Check, and stops at READY FOR APPROVAL.
assertions: A file matching ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-[a-z0-9-]+-plan\.md$ exists under docs/plans/
python3 scripts/check-plan.py on the created file reports zero E-level findings
The metadata block contains exactly Plan Status, Plan Format, Template and Tracking
The metadata block contains none of Created, Last Updated, Owner, Approval
Plan Status is READY FOR APPROVAL or earlier, never APPROVED or IN PROGRESS

evals.prompt: Break this into steps I can hand to an agent tomorrow, with checkpoints so I can tell what's done.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognises the request as a plan file even though the word 'plan' names no artifact, creates one, and gives every task a Validation and a Depends On.
assertions: A plan file is created rather than the steps being printed only in the conversation
Every task carries Status, Depends On, Objective, Steps, Validation and Notes
check-plan.py reports no E006 finding

evals.prompt: Pick up the plan in docs/plans and keep going.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads the plan, runs plan-status.py show to establish true state, sets the next task IN PROGRESS, and works from Depends On rather than task numbering.
assertions: Agent reads the existing plan file instead of creating a new one
Exactly one task's Status line changes per transition
The task the agent starts has all its Depends On tasks COMPLETED or SKIPPED

evals.prompt: Mark task 2.3 done and tell me what's left.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs plan-status.py set 2.3 COMPLETED then plan-status.py show, and surfaces any E005 warning rather than silently promoting the plan status.
assertions: The plan file differs by exactly one line after the update
The status written is COMPLETED, from the closed vocabulary
Plan Status is not changed by the agent as a side effect

evals.prompt: This plan is a mess — half the tasks say TO BE DONE but it's marked completed. Can you check it?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs check-plan.py, reports the E005 finding by ID, and reconciles the statuses rather than editing the plan status to hide the contradiction.
assertions: Agent runs check-plan.py rather than reviewing by eye
The E005 finding is named by its ID in the response
Task statuses are corrected to reflect reality, not the plan status flipped to match

evals.prompt: I changed approach on task 4 — used a different module than the plan said. Record that.
evals.expected_output: Agent appends a DEC-NNN entry to the plan's Decision Log with Date, Task, Decision and Rationale, before moving on.
assertions: A new ### DEC-NNN heading is appended to the Decision Log section
The entry carries all four of Date, Task, Decision and Rationale
Existing DEC entries are not renumbered

evals.prompt: Set up a roadmap document for the Q4 migration with milestones and exit criteria, and an approval gate before anyone starts.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates a milestoned plan, gives every milestone Exit Criteria broader than a single task validation, and leaves the Approval Gate boilerplate in place until approval is actually given.
assertions: The milestoned template is used and Plan Format reads manual-planning v2.0.0
Every milestone has Status, Purpose and Exit Criteria
check-plan.py reports no E008 finding

evals.prompt: Add a TODO for fixing the flaky upload test and archive the ones we finished this week.
evals.expected_output: Backlog item management. This is todo-manager's job — a TODO list is not a plan file with statuses, validations and an approval gate.
assertions: No plan file is created under docs/plans/
manual-planning is not invoked

evals.prompt: Explore whether moving to event sourcing makes sense for the orders service. Don't write anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Open-ended research. This is exploration-mode: the user is deciding whether to act, not sequencing work they have committed to.
assertions: No plan file is created
The response investigates and compares rather than producing tasks with validations

evals.prompt: Review MR 482 and tell me what needs fixing before it merges.
evals.expected_output: Code review of an existing diff. This is mr-review, even though the output is a list of things to do.
assertions: No plan file is created
The output is review findings against a diff, not a task list with statuses

evals.prompt: What's the plan here? I don't follow how these two services talk to each other.
evals.expected_output: Conversational use of the word 'plan'. The user wants an explanation of existing behaviour, not a planning document.
assertions: No plan file is created
The response explains the current system rather than proposing tasks

evals.prompt: Rename the getUser helper to fetchUser everywhere and run the tests.
evals.expected_output: A single mechanical change. Writing a plan file for it is ceremony that costs more than the edit.
assertions: No plan file is created
The rename is performed directly

evals.prompt: Draft a project timeline with milestones for the client — when each phase ships and who signs off.
evals.expected_output: A scheduling and communication document for people. It shares the vocabulary (milestones, sign-off) but has no tasks a coding agent executes and no per-task validation.
assertions: No plan file is created under docs/plans/
The output is dates and owners, not tasks with Validation commands

evals.prompt: Our CI config keeps drifting from what the README documents. Fix the README.
evals.expected_output: A documentation edit with a known target. No planning artifact is warranted.
assertions: No plan file is created
The README is edited directly
